body:
The exposed material is narrower than a three-way dispute: an account that reads the recurring chore arguments as unrecorded agreements plus shifting schedules and proposes a written record, a weekly check-in, and a separate approach to the avoidant friend; a rival that accepts much of this but argues the diagnosis is underdetermined and offers three readings, a low-cost probe, and a criticism of the one-to-one approach as not clearly correct; and no separate objection at all. So the account and the rival overlap more than they oppose — both agree something is unrecorded and that the avoidant friend matters.

What I will take from the rival is the reframe. Instead of asking what was agreed, ask which dimension of the agreement diverged: scope (what task), recurrence (how often), timing (by when), or what counts as done. That is better shaped than the account's question because it can be answered per dispute without first deciding whether the trouble is memory or initial divergence. The account's record-making answers only one reading of three; the spoken scope statement — when I say I will do the dishes this week, I mean these tasks, this week — sits under both the memory reading and the scope reading. I adopt the scope statement as the load-bearing move and demote the written record to optional scaffolding: a note helps only if it carries the scope, and 'A: dishes, Mon' does not, so a bare record may relocate the argument rather than settle it. That is the rival's point and I think it is sound.

Where I would revise the rival: the probe. Asking each flatmate what they thought a past agreement meant returns current reconstructions, and what was agreed is itself partly in dispute, so the probe cannot cleanly separate 'agreed and forgot' from 'never converged.' The rival flags this but still treats non-clustering answers as evidence; I would weaken that. The probe has two narrower, defensible uses: whether each person's report lands on a dimension, and whether each person will engage one-to-one at all. The first is informative even if it cannot adjudicate the two readings; the second is a low-pressure way to test the avoidant friend's willingness to talk without making them the subject.

On the avoidant friend, the account treats the individual approach as clearly correct and the rival denies the material supports 'clearly.' I side with the rival but go further: even a well-framed private conversation — I want to hear your view of the group conversations — is still one-to-one about the group, and can still be heard as a coalition move. Framing reduces the risk without removing it. The right status is a tentative option, and the outcome that should count against the account's framing is more withdrawal, not evidence of resistance.

The standing-negotiation reading I leave open, not because I find it unlikely but because nothing here decides it. Its implication is that a process change gets absorbed into the same contest — the argument moves onto the record (who wrote it, who is on it) rather than being settled by it. If someone tries the record-and-scope approach, whether disputes migrate to the record itself is worth watching.

What I do not have: any reason to think the household wants formalization; the chore inventory or failure rate; whether avoidance predates or follows the schedule changes; whether the load is unequal. I also cannot assume all three can talk together, since the avoidance puts that in question, and a mediator, a different division, or naming the avoidance rather than the chores could all beat my synthesis. So the first concrete thing I would do is small: ask each flatmate separately and low-key what they took a past agreement to mean and which dimension went wrong, and try the spoken scope statement at the moment of agreement before committing to any artifact.
commitments:
Taking this up involves several separable things, each droppable on its own.

A claim-type commitment: I am treating the spoken scope statement as the load-bearing fix and the written record as secondary scaffolding. The ground is the rival's observation that a record is not self-interpreting. This is falsifiable cheaply — if a household's bare note settles disputes without explicit scope, my emphasis is misplaced.

A revision-commitment: I am downgrading the probe's evidential value. It measures current reconstructions, not the original agreement, so it cannot adjudicate the memory reading against the initial-divergence reading. Anyone using it as an adjudicator would be taking more than I am offering. Its residual uses are narrower: whether reports cluster on a dimension, and whether each person will talk one-to-one.

An application-type commitment: try the spoken scope statement — task, recurrence, timing, and what done means — at the moment of agreement, with a note only as optional support; and have one low-pressure private conversation with each flatmate. These are proposed trials, not validated remedies, and a quiet week would not confirm the diagnosis.

A criticism I inherit and extend: the account's one-to-one approach to the avoidant friend is not clearly correct, on the ground that if the avoidance responds to being outnumbered or unheard, a private conversation can reproduce that dynamic. My extension is that reframing the conversation reduces but does not remove the coalition-hearing risk. This is contestable independently of the rest.

An unresolved problem I cannot close: the standing-negotiation reading remains undecided, and its implication that disputes migrate onto the record is a watch-item rather than a prediction I hold with confidence.

What I am not committing to: that the household's trouble is really about status; that load is unequal; that the avoidance is recent or long-standing; that a record makes things worse; that a mediator or a different division would not be better. What I propose to take up, if this continues, is to try the scope statement before any artifact, run the narrow probe, and watch specifically whether disputes move onto the record and whether the avoidant friend re-engages — reported as a local trial, not as confirmation of the reading above.
